headline: Today's bike is 2.3 km longer than one you already rode a week ago - the 35 minutes after it is the whole experiment.
body:
This is not a distance test. On **29 August you rode 82.7 km with 1,338 m of climbing** - 16 m/km against race day's 6 - and the brick run died with the battery. Today's 85 km is **2.32 km** more than that. The run is the only part of this you have never done with data.

Bike at **140-150 bpm, 28-31 km/h on the flat**, cap **155 on the climbs**, keep pedalling over the top. Then straight off, no sitting down: **35 min at 6:45-7:00/km, 145-155 bpm**. Fuel **80-90 g/hr** - two bottles at 90 g, two gels.

The gate is yours to call this morning. training.json still ends at **Wednesday's 08:16 pull, 72 hours old**, so I cannot see last night's HRV. The last four readings were all Unbalanced, bottoming at **48 against a 14-day mean of 61**. Under 61 on the watch: ride at **135-145 bpm** and keep every minute of the run. Under 55: cut the bike to **65 km** and still run the full 35.

Ankle, before you go?
